learn.hook: A train can carry more than 1000 people! Let's meet the big 4-digit numbers.
points: 999 + 1 = 1000. It is the smallest 4-digit number. We read it as 'one thousand'.
10 hundreds make 1 thousand. 100 tens also make 1 thousand.
We read 3405 as 'three thousand four hundred five'. A 0 in a place means nothing is there.
Counting on by 1000 changes only the thousands digit: 2345, 3345, 4345.
learn.reallife: Prices of bicycles, the number of pages in a big book and people in a stadium are often 4-digit numbers.

games.title: Match the number to its name

quiz.q: What is 999 + 1?
quiz.explain: 999 is the biggest 3-digit number. One more makes 1000, the smallest 4-digit number.
quiz.mistake: Writes the 1 next to 999 instead of adding

quiz.q: How many hundreds make 1 thousand?
quiz.explain: 100 + 100 + ... ten times = 1000. So 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'how many hundreds' with 'how many tens'

quiz.q: Write 'three thousand four hundred five' in numerals.
quiz.explain: 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones make 3405.
steps: No tens, so put 0 in the tens place: 3405
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the tens place, or writes each word as a separate number

quiz.q: How do we read 6080?
quiz.explain: 6080 has 6 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens and 0 ones. That is six thousand eighty.
quiz.mistake: Reads the 8 as hundreds instead of tens

quiz.q: What is 1 more than 4999?
quiz.explain: 4999 + 1 = 5000. All the 9s turn to 0s and the thousands digit goes up by 1.
steps: The carry moves through tens and hundreds
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 to the hundreds place instead of the ones place

quiz.q: What is 100 more than 2950?
quiz.explain: Adding 100 adds 1 to the hundreds. 9 hundreds + 1 hundred = 10 hundreds = 1 thousand. So 2950 becomes 3050.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 100, or adds 1000

quiz.q: Arjun counts on by thousands: 2345, 3345, 4345, ? What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each time the thousands digit goes up by 1. 4345 + 1000 = 5345.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 or 100 instead of 1000

quiz.q: What is the smallest 4-digit number?
quiz.explain: 999 has only 3 digits. The first number with 4 digits is 1000.
quiz.mistake: Picks 999, which is the biggest 3-digit number

teach.ask: Gappu counted 999 grains and then found one more. What number is that, and why is it special?
teach.praise: Hooray! 999 and 1 more is 1000, the first 4-digit number, made of 10 hundreds. Gappu is amazed!
teach.nudge: How many digits does the new number have? How many hundreds are inside it?

learn.hook: In 4725, the 7 is worth 700, not just 7! Where a digit sits decides its value.
points: A 4-digit number has 4 places: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
In 4725: 4 thousands, 7 hundreds, 2 tens and 5 ones.
Place value = digit × the value of its place. The 7 in 4725 is worth 7 × 100 = 700.
A 0 keeps a place empty: 3047 has 0 hundreds.

example.q: Meena has two ₹1000 notes, five ₹100 notes and three ₹10 notes. How much money is that?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers count ₹1000, ₹100 and ₹10 notes in bundles, just like thousands, hundreds and tens.

items.text: In 1958, the digit in the tens place is ___.

quiz.q: What is the place value of 7 in 4725?
quiz.explain: The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 × 100 = 700.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit itself (face value) instead of its place value

quiz.q: What number is 5000 + 300 + 20 + 6?
quiz.explain: 5 thousands, 3 hundreds, 2 tens and 6 ones make 5326.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Which digit is in the tens place of 8309?
quiz.explain: 8309 = 8 thousands, 3 hundreds, 0 tens, 9 ones. The tens digit is 0.
quiz.mistake: Reads the places from the left and picks the second digit

quiz.q: What number has 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones?
quiz.explain: Write each digit in its place: 3 | 0 | 4 | 7 = 3047.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 0 for the hundreds place

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 6158?
quiz.explain: 6 thousands = 6000, 1 hundred = 100, 5 tens = 50, 8 ones = 8.
quiz.mistake: Writes the tens digit as ones (5 instead of 50)

quiz.q: Meena has two ₹1000 notes, five ₹100 notes and three ₹10 notes. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ₹10 notes, or puts digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: Which number has 9 in the hundreds place?
quiz.explain: In 2934 the places are 2 thousands, 9 hundreds, 3 tens, 4 ones.
quiz.mistake: Picks the number that starts with 9 (that 9 is in the thousands place)

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 1000?
quiz.explain: 10 tens make 100, and 10 hundreds make 1000. So 1000 has 10 × 10 = 100 tens.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there are only 10 tens in a thousand

teach.ask: Gappu says the 7 in 4725 is just worth 7. Is Gappu right? Please explain!
teach.praise: Oh! The 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 700. Place decides value. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which place is the 7 sitting in? What does that place mean?

learn.hook: Riya's school has 1450 students and Arjun's has 1405. Which school is bigger? Let's compare!
points: A number with more digits is bigger: any 4-digit number is bigger than any 3-digit number.
If both have 4 digits, compare the thousands first. If they are the same, compare the hundreds, then tens, then ones.
We use > for 'greater than', < for 'less than' and = for 'equal to'.
To make the biggest number from some digits, put the biggest digit first. For the smallest, put the smallest digit first (but not 0).
learn.reallife: We compare prices of phones, scores in a quiz and heights of mountains using the same steps.

games.title: Greater or smaller?
items: Hundreds are the same (6). Tens: 0 < 2, so 5602 is smaller.
999 has 3 digits and 1000 has 4, so 1000 is bigger.
Both numbers are exactly the same.

quiz.q: Which number is greater: 4567 or 4657?
quiz.explain: The thousands are the same. In the hundreds, 6 > 5, so 4657 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Compares the ones digits first (7 = 7) and gets confused

quiz.q: Which is the largest? 3098, 3890, 3809, 3980
quiz.explain: All have 3 thousands. The hundreds digits are 0, 8, 8, 9. 3980 has 9 hundreds, so it is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the last digit instead of the first different place

quiz.q: Use the digits 5, 2, 8 and 1 once each. What is the largest 4-digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the digits from biggest to smallest: 8, 5, 2, 1. That makes 8521.
quiz.mistake: Does not put every digit in biggest-to-smallest order

quiz.q: Use the digits 5, 2, 8 and 1 once each. What is the smallest 4-digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the digits from smallest to biggest: 1, 2, 5, 8. That makes 1258.
quiz.mistake: Puts the smallest digit first but mixes up the rest

quiz.q: Which sign goes in the box? 7001 ☐ 7010
quiz.explain: Thousands and hundreds are the same. Tens: 0 < 1, so 7001 < 7010.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number ending in 1 is bigger than a number ending in 0

quiz.q: Riya's school has 1450 students. Arjun's school has 1405 students. How many more students are in Riya's school?
quiz.mistake: Takes away wrongly and gets 55

quiz.q: Which number comes just before 6000?
quiz.explain: Just before means 1 less. 6000 - 1 = 5999.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1000 or 100 instead of 1

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to largest?
quiz.explain: Compare the hundreds: 0 < 4 = 4 < 5. Then 2405 < 2450 because 0 tens < 5 tens.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the first two digits

teach.ask: Gappu has 5602 seeds and Kabir has 5620. Gappu thinks they have the same. How do we compare?
teach.praise: I see! Start from the thousands, and when digits match, move to the next place. 5620 is bigger!
teach.nudge: Which place should Gappu look at first? What if those digits are the same?
